priority: Separate speech activity from interruption decisions before model and provider cancellation work

compatibility.microphone.barge_in_trigger=vad: mode=vad and min_words=0 unless explicitly overridden
compatibility.microphone.barge_in_trigger=word: mode=vad and min_words=1 unless explicitly overridden
compatibility.write_policy: New UI writes use microphone.interruption keys; runtime retains legacy reads during migration

proposed_owners.responsibility: Emit speech activity evidence and timestamps only
Own overlap identity, eligibility, decision, timer and bounded STT gate
Own authoritative conversation context and conditional committed transition
Report response-scoped local playout state; no claim of human reception
Return interruption, backchannel or inconclusive for one overlap ID

transcript_gate.opens_when: Adaptive mode has an active overlap for the current context and local playout response
transcript_gate.positive: Commit interruption, rotate context once, replay held STT in order into the new context
transcript_gate.negative: Classify backchannel, discard held overlap STT, preserve assistant response
transcript_gate.inconclusive: After eligibility, fail toward user input and replay held STT
transcript_gate.overflow: Commit eligible interruption and release STT; never silently discard user input
transcript_gate.late_result: Ignore unless context ID, overlap ID and local playout response ID all match

required_tests: VAD activity never directly emits interruption commands
Duration below, at and above 0.5 seconds
Word count below, at and above configured threshold
Positive decision replays held STT once into the committed turn
Negative decision discards only the matching overlap STT
Inconclusive, timeout and overflow fail toward user input
Late and duplicate decisions cannot affect a newer overlap
Adaptive mode requires matching local playout response
Legacy VAD and word settings map to the new options
UI and runtime defaults remain equal
Greeting protection and EOS behavior remain compatible
risks: No current adapter-visible local playout boundary
VAD providers may report onset and duration differently
Cross-lane VAD and STT events can arrive in either order
A transcript gate can lose user input if bounds and fallback are wrong
Adaptive provider latency can make interruption slower than VAD
Remote audio classification changes privacy and credential boundaries
Changing the default effective delay can regress barge-in latency
A late decision can corrupt a newer turn without overlap identity checks
rollback: Disable adaptive mode, restore legacy option writes, and revert the complete activity/decision contract, gate and channel capability change as one unit. No schema migration is required.
open_decisions: Exact adaptive decision provider and privacy contract
Exact WebRTC and telephony files providing local playout evidence
Whether 0.5 seconds becomes the effective default immediately or through staged rollout
Gate event, byte and duration bounds
Initial channels permitted to enable adaptive mode
